title: Hardgroove 1 · tom pickups
text: Keep quarter-note kicks with the right hand. Place each low tom one sixteenth before the next kick. Count 1 e & a aloud. Start slowly; first listen to the two sounds answering each other.

intro.goal: Keep the kick steady while the other hand anticipates each beat.
intro.watch: The tom lands on a, not on the next beat. Keep the hand relaxed; do not rush the following kick.

resources.name: Hardgroove drum construction · Jon Musgrave

title: Hardgroove 2 · open-hat drive
text: Keep the kick and tom pattern from lesson 1. Add open hats on every &. The right hand moves between Kick R and Open hat; the left hand keeps the tom pickups.

intro.goal: Add an offbeat hat without moving the tom or kick.
intro.watch: The hat comes before the tom: & then a then the next kick. Think of three evenly spaced sixteenth positions.

resources.name: Hardgroove drum construction · Jon Musgrave

title: Hardgroove 3 · clap accents
text: Add claps on beats 2 and 4. Keep the right-hand kick steady and the left-hand tom pickups intact. Listen to the louder clap accents and the softer tom answers.

intro.goal: Keep the rolling pattern stable when the clap joins.
intro.watch: Clap and kick land together on 2 and 4. Let both hands arrive together; the tom just before them stays separate.

resources.name: Hardgroove drum construction · Jon Musgrave

title: Hardgroove 4 · the return
text: Play four bars. Bar 2 shifts just one tom from a to & after beat 2. Bar 4 adds a high-tom answer on 4 & before the low tom on 4 a. Let the next kick start the phrase again. Loop bars 2 or 4 first, then turn the section loop off for a full run.

intro.goal: Remember a four-bar phrase and return to beat 1 after a short tom answer.
intro.watch: At the end of bar 4, the open hat and high tom land together on 4 &. Do not add a fifth beat.

resources.name: Hardgroove drum construction · Jon Musgrave

title: Broken techno 1 · missing kick
text: Keep hats on every & and snares on beats 2 and 4. Kicks land on 1, 2 a and 3 &. Count through beats that have no kick.

intro.goal: Hold a steady pulse when the kick leaves the quarter-note grid.
intro.watch: The second kick is just before beat 3. A silent downbeat is intentional; do not fill it with an extra kick.

title: Broken techno 2 · rim pickup
text: Keep lesson 1 unchanged and add a right-hand rim on 4 a. The hat on 4 & comes first, then the rim, then the kick on the next 1.

intro.goal: Add a pickup at the end of the bar without shortening the bar.
intro.watch: The rim is a sixteenth before the next kick. Do not press rim and kick together.

resources.name: Progressive techno layers · Attack Magazine
Broken UK techno beat · Future Music

title: Broken techno 3 · two kicks
text: Alternate two bars. In bar 1, the middle kick is on 2 a; in bar 2 it moves earlier to 2 &. Hats, snares and the final rim stay the same. Learn the kick changes alone, then add the other layers.

intro.goal: Alternate two kick shapes while the other parts stay steady.
intro.watch: Bar 2 has kick and hat together on 2 &. It is a deliberate change, not a timing mistake.

title: Broken techno 4 · the return
text: Keep alternating the two kick shapes across four bars. In bar 4, leave out the final closed hat and play rim answers on 4 e and 4 a. Count the missing hat silently. Return to the kick on 1. Practise bar 4 as a section, then finish a full run.

intro.goal: Keep a four-bar form through an intentional gap and a rim answer.
intro.watch: The final bar replaces the hat on 4 & with silence. An extra hat there counts as an extra hit.

title: UK funky 1 · syncopated rim
text: Start with a four-beat kick. Put the rim on 2 & and on beat 4. Count every beat even though the rim gives the pattern a different shape.

intro.goal: Place a syncopated rim over a steady dance pulse.
intro.watch: The first rim is between beats 2 and 3. The second rim lands together with the kick on beat 4.

Speed garage production · The Producer School

title: UK funky 2 · hats and rim
text: Add hats on every &. At 2 &, press Hat R and Rim together with your right hand. Elsewhere the same hand plays the two pads separately. Keep the kick steady.

intro.goal: Combine a same-hand chord with a continuing offbeat line.
intro.watch: At 2 &, rim and hat are one simultaneous event. Prepare both pads so neither is late.

Speed garage production · The Producer School

title: Speed garage 1 · the skippy top
text: Switch to a clap on 2 and 4. Keep open hats on every & and add short closed hats on 1 a and 3 a. Bar 2 ends with one extra kick on 4 a. Listen to each layer first; this first exercise uses a straight grid.

intro.goal: Keep a dance pulse under a skippy two-bar hat and kick phrase.
intro.watch: Each closed hat follows an open hat by one sixteenth. Let the final kick of bar 2 lead into the next bar; do not merge the two kicks.

resources.name: UK funky drum example · UK Bass Tutorials
Speed garage production · The Producer School

title: Speed garage 2 · fill, restart
text: Play the two-bar idea as a four-bar phrase. Bar 3 adds one quiet closed hat on 2 a. In bar 4, replace the clap on 4 with a short snare answer on 4, 4 & and 4 a. Keep the kick under it, then return to 1. This is a straight-grid foundation; fine shuffle is not scored separately.

intro.goal: Finish a four-bar club phrase with a snare answer and a clean restart.
intro.watch: Kick and snare land together on beat 4. The following two snares are not evenly spaced triplets.
